fields.title: A security requirement arrives as a review comment

sections.What we are doing instead:
A security requirement arrives as a comment on a pull request, from the maintainer who also wrote the change. Nothing identifies a change as higher risk before the work starts, and nothing records how a change could be attacked.

`.github/SECURITY.md` says how CI contains what it runs, and states what is in scope for a report. It covers the repository as a whole, and no change is weighed against it.
sections.Why we need it: Threat modelling a documentation tool that reads a repository and writes files back into it produces a short list, and `.github/SECURITY.md` already contains it. Turning that into a risk triage and a design review for each change is real work. One person in the author, reviewer and approver roles gets little from the separation.
sections.What the risk is: A change ships with a security fault that nobody sorted it for. The workflows deny by default and the analysers fail a build, so the arrangement is right and unstated. What slips through is a fault the same person misses twice, as author and as reviewer. A triage step filled in by that person would miss it a third time.
sections.What compensates:
* [std-CI](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/01c2db7153b064d26441c61b1aa8dd22e4dac7f7/examples/dog-fooding/standards/workflows.md) limits each job to the least permission it needs. [ctl-0015](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/01c2db7153b064d26441c61b1aa8dd22e4dac7f7/examples/dog-fooding/controls/0015-zizmor.md) fails a workflow granting more than read at its
  top level, and a reviewer checks that each job uses the permission it declares.
* `.github/SECURITY.md` is public, so a reader can see what CI contains and where a report is in scope.
* `eng:std-CSSTY` turns the analysers on, so their security rules fail a build without a reviewer looking.
sections.How it closes: A standard says which changes count as high risk here. It requires such a change to record its security requirements, and how it could be attacked, before it is built. It cites `.github/SECURITY.md` as the threat statement for the repository. This record closes on that standard.
sections.Scope: The `kac` tool, the workflows, and the documentation site's build.
